attachments.origin_landmark: anococcygeal ligament and the tip of the coccyx
attachments.insertion_landmark: perineal body (a midline structure; the right hip bone is named only because the schema takes one insertion)

innervation.root_levels: S2-S4 (inferior rectal branch of the pudendal nerve)

actions: contracts reflexly on rises in intra-abdominal pressure

functional_compartments.name: Subcutaneous part
functional_compartments.function_note: Encircles the anal orifice just beneath the skin; its contraction is the anal wink reflex used to test S2-S4 integrity.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Superficial part
functional_compartments.function_note: Elliptical, anchored between the perineal body and the coccyx -- the only part with bony attachment.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Deep part
functional_compartments.function_note: Blends with puborectalis above. Puborectalis maintains the anorectal angle, which contributes more to gross continence than sphincter tone alone; the two are damaged together in obstetric injury.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not routinely ultrasound-guided: injected directly under digital or anoscopic guidance. Most surgeons target the internal anal sphincter (not this muscle) for chronic anal fissure, but the intersphincteric groove between the two sphincters is the shared landmark; standard practice places two to four injection points around the anal circumference (commonly the lateral quadrants, avoiding the anterior/posterior midline where the fissure usually lies), either directly into the fissure edges ('out of the fissure' site) or into the sphincter on each side of the fissure ('side of the fissure' site).
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Anal canal wall, at or just deep to the intersphincteric groove; the operator's other hand or an anoscope stabilizes/visualizes the canal during injection.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: The chronic fissure itself (usually posterior midline) and the visible/palpable intersphincteric groove between internal and external sphincter are the landmarks used to place injections relative to the fissure.
structures_at_risk: internal anal sphincter, immediately deep/medial to this muscle and the more physiologically relevant target for the fissure's underlying hypertonicity
anal mucosa overlying the fissure, at risk of direct injection if 'out of the fissure' sites are used imprecisely
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Botulinum toxin for chronic anal fissure is a well-established, widely practiced alternative to lateral internal sphincterotomy. A network meta-analysis of 27 RCTs (1880 patients) found low-dose toxin injected 'out of the fissure' gave better short-term healing while injection to each side of the fissure reduced longer-term recurrence; a national US survey of colorectal surgeons found 90% use 50-100 U, with a majority injecting into the internal sphincter in four quadrants. Because most published dosing targets the internal sphincter specifically, the technique is recorded here for the external sphincter as the adjacent structure most surgeons deliberately avoid overtreating, rather than as this muscle's own primary target.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Vitoopinyoparb K et al.
